evidence: tokenInput is a local page-level ref (bot.vue:20) — not in Pinia state, not on botStore.current.
On successful connect, tokenInput.value = '' (bot.vue:49) clears the local ref.
botStore.connect(projectId, token) receives token only as a positional arg — store body (bot.ts:39-63) places it in the POST body only; never on state, never returned, never in URL.

Error path: only apiError(err, 'bot.connect') runs (bot.vue:51,75,89). useApiError returns i18n strings keyed by status code — never inserts err.options.body or response.body into the user-visible message.
ofetch body redaction in store (bot.ts:59-60) replaces err.options.body with '[redacted]' before re-throwing, so even callers that log the whole error object cannot leak the secret.
Token is never interpolated into a URL, query string, route param, log statement, or surviving reactive ref.
Vitest spec asserts wrapper.text() !~ TOKEN_REGEX after a 422 error path (bot.spec.ts:347-362).
The middle glyph is the literal U+2022 BULLET character repeated three times — no JS escape sequence, no \u202… substitution.
Only the last 3 chars (tokenSuffix from API) appear; backend never sends the body, so the secret remains undisclosed.
Spec asserts the exact rendered text '1234567890:•••...xyz' (bot.spec.ts:176, 371).
Modal body uses t('bot.disconnect.modal.body', { username: botStore.current?.telegramUsername ?? '' }) (bot.vue:185-191) — canonical i18n key with {username} interpolation.
uk.json body: 'Відключити бота @{username}? Вхідні повідомлення припиняться, а вебхук буде видалено. Підключити знову можна будь-коли.'
en.json body: 'Disconnect bot @{username}? Incoming messages will stop and the webhook will be removed. You can reconnect anytime.'
Username is rendered via Vue {{ }} interpolation inside DialogDescription — HTML-encoded by default; no XSS surface even if username were attacker-shaped.
Spec asserts modal text contains '@SmokeBot' and the canonical phrase (bot.spec.ts:265-279).

useApiError builds candidates as `errors.${contextKey}.${status}` then `errors.${contextKey}.generic` then `errors.generic` — pure i18n key resolution. No interpolation of error.body, response.body, response.data, err.message, etc.
Error display in template (bot.vue:174-176) uses {{ errorMessage }} via Vue text interpolation — HTML-encoded, no v-html.
Store-level redaction of err.options.body (bot.ts:59-60) provides defense-in-depth for any caller that decides to console.log the rejected error.

findings.title: Bot-token input uses type="text" instead of type="password"
findings.description: The token input is `<input id="bot-token" v-model="tokenInput" type="text" autocomplete="off" spellcheck="false" …>` (bot.vue:112-122). The token is a long-lived bearer credential for the Telegram Bot API. Rendering it as visible plaintext exposes it to shoulder-surfing, screen-share leaks, and screenshot artifacts during the connect flow. Using `type="password"` would mask the characters by default while keeping paste support intact. autocomplete="off" is correctly set, but masking is independent of autofill behaviour.
findings.impact: Live token visible on screen while typing/pasting; risk multiplied if user records a demo, shares their screen, or works in a public space. Not an AC17 violation (the token still never leaves the browser) but reduces the practical secrecy of the token at the user-interface boundary.
findings.recommendation: Change to `type="password"`. If product wants a 'show token' toggle for usability, add a separate button that flips type between password↔text and resets to password on blur/unmount. Example: `<input :type="reveal ? 'text' : 'password'" …>` with `reveal` defaulting to false.

findings.title: Token persists in input ref after a failed connect attempt
findings.description: onConnect (bot.vue:42-55) clears `tokenInput.value` only on the success path (line 49). When connect rejects (400/409/422/429/500/502), the token remains both in the reactive ref and as the DOM input's `.value` until the user manually clears it or navigates away. While AC17 specifically governs leakage OUTSIDE the user's browser, the persistence widens the window in which Vue Devtools / DOM inspection / screenshot artifacts retain the secret.
findings.impact: Slightly longer lifetime of the bearer token in client memory and in the DOM after an error. UX trade-off (user may want to fix a typo without re-pasting), but secrets handling typically prefers explicit clearing.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) clear `tokenInput.value` in the catch block as well (forces re-paste on retry, but maximally tight); or (b) accept the current UX and document the trade-off explicitly in a code comment so future maintainers don't 'helpfully' bind tokenInput to anywhere else. The status quo is defensible — no change is strictly required.

findings.title: Empty-string fallback in modal body interpolation can render '@ '
findings.description: Modal renders `t('bot.disconnect.modal.body', { username: botStore.current?.telegramUsername ?? '' })` (bot.vue:187-189). If `botStore.current` becomes null while the modal is open (e.g., the projects-store watcher in bot.ts:75-86 clears `current` on project switch, or a stale-current 404 fires), the interpolation produces `@ ` followed by the rest of the sentence — confusing UX rather than a security issue, but it's a leakage of an inconsistent state to the user.
findings.impact: Cosmetic/UX, no exploitation path. Worth a defensive check: if `botStore.current` is null while the modal is open, the modal should auto-close rather than render an empty `@`. Not a security finding strictly, included for completeness because it relates to the AC19 copy.
findings.recommendation: Add `watch(() => botStore.current, (v) => { if (!v) showDisconnectModal.value = false })` near the existing setup script, or gate the Dialog `open` prop on `showDisconnectModal && !!botStore.current`. Optional hardening; do not block on this.

non_findings_explicitly_checked: Token in URL/query/route — not present; `useApi()<Bot>(\`/api/v1/projects/${projectId}/bot/connect\`, { method: 'POST', body: { token } })` keeps token in body only.
Token in Pinia state — botStore.$state only exposes `current: Bot|null`; `inFlight` is a module-scoped closure and the connect function does not write the token to any reactive holder.
Token in console.log/console.error — no log statements in bot.vue or bot.ts; the only console.warn is on a 404 stale-current path that does not touch the token (useApi.ts:73).
XSS via telegramUsername/telegramFirstName/tokenSuffix — all rendered via Vue {{ }} text interpolation; no v-html; HTML-encoded by default. Safe.
XSS via i18n message interpolation — vue-i18n by default HTML-escapes interpolated values; no <i18n-t> with t-component slots used.

CSRF — useApi.ts:99-103 adds X-XSRF-TOKEN header from the XSRF-TOKEN cookie for non-safe methods (POST connect/disconnect/test-message). Spring CookieServerCsrfTokenRepository pairing is documented in the composable. Protected.
Authz — frontend correctly delegates authorization to backend on `/api/v1/projects/{projectId}/bot/*`. No client-side gate is acceptable for a SPA when the server enforces it.

Hardcoded secrets — no embedded API keys, tokens, passwords, or connection strings in any of the audited files. The fixture token `1234567890:AAFakeTokenABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ` in bot.spec.ts is a test-only string explicitly named 'Fake' and only used inside the test runner.
Insecure deserialization — N/A; only $fetch JSON parsing of trusted-shape responses.
Vulnerable components — out of scope for this delta; not changed by Task 9.
Disconnect operation does not re-prompt for confirmation outside the modal — modal copy itself satisfies AC19; double-confirm not required.
